summary: Keepalive reconnect flood causing elevated 5xx rates and upstream runtime blockage for BrightChat
description: Issue summary: BrightChat reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses (502/503) on their chat streaming route (/v1/chat/stream) starting ~2026-03-10 18:30 UTC. Impact: ~18% error rate across their tenant for 20 minutes, user-facing disconnects, and message duplication from client retries. Environment: BrightChat on Dedicated pool in us-east-1. Behavior: API gateway returned rapid 502/503 spikes; upstream runtime processes entered a blocked state with high thread counts and elevated syscall wait times. Support notes: customer observed multiple mobile clients rapidly reconnecting after a mobile SDK update.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate ~2000 short-lived websocket reconnects to /v1/chat/stream over ~2 minutes from the same tenant. 2) Monitor API gateway 5xx rate and upstream runtime thread blocking and accept_queue length. 3) Observe keepalive pool exhaustion and increased fd usage on ephemeral proxies. Expected: graceful handling and bounded 5xx; Observed: accept_queue growth, rapid apigw 502/503s, runtime watchdog kills and restart loops.
logs:
- apigw logs (2026-03-10T18:30:12Z): upstream response 502
- runtime stderr (2026-03-10T18:30:22Z): threadpool busy=256/256 blocked_on=socket_read
- ephemeral-proxy (2026-03-10T18:31:05Z): fd_count=8192 (~90% of soft limit)
- kernel: accept_queue backlog=512 -> sustained for 3m
- runtime watchdog: triggered SIGTERM for pid 6371 due to slow mainloop (gc pause not to blame)
metrics_observed:
- apigw 5xx rate: baseline 0.3% -> peak 18%
- accept_queue length: baseline 10 -> peak 520
- ephemeral-proxy fd usage: baseline 1200 -> peak 8200
- runtime thread count: baseline 48 -> peak 260
- runtime syscall wait (epoll_wait): median latency increased from 2ms -> 120ms
- GPU usage: normal (no NVML resets observed)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 19:00 - Initial triage by Support (Aisha): correlated customer-reported timeframe with apigw error spike and accept_queue growth in us-east-1.
2026-03-10 19:20 - SRE (Diego): attached live pcap and epoll traces; observed many half-closed sockets from the same client IP ranges, repeated reconnects with very short session durations (<2s).

2026-03-10 19:45 - Runtime team (Lena Chen): inspected runtime stack traces; mainloop blocked trying to read from socket fds that were in a half-closed state; threadpool backlog prevented timely processing, causing watchdog to restart runtimes.

2026-03-10 20:10 - Hypothesis: client SDK regression removed proper Connection: close semantics and exponential backoff, leading to reconnect storm and half-open sockets that stall epoll and exhaust ephemeral proxy fd pools.
2026-03-10 20:30 - Evidence: BrightChat provided SDK release notes indicating a change to keepalive behavior at 2026-03-10T18:25Z. Timing matches incident window.

2026-03-11 02:00 - Temporary mitigation tested: applied ingress short-live connection filter and increased ephemeral-proxy fd soft limit in the affected cluster; apigw 5xx dropped to 1.2% within 10 minutes.
2026-03-11 03:10 - Runtime patch prepared: add defensive handling for half-closed sockets (close-on-epoll-hang) and early return on excessive short-lived sessions per-tenant; PR: runtime/#1423.
2026-03-11 08:00 - Follow-up monitoring: alert added for accept_queue > 200 sustained for 1m and fd usage > 75% on ephemeral proxies for dedicated pools.
Notes: No evidence of GPU driver or model-induced OOMs; issue is network/accept-queue and socket lifecycle related.
comments: 2026-03-10 19:05 - Aisha (Support): Opened ticket after initial customer report. Added apigw and runtime logs. Asked BrightChat for SDK version and any recent client changes.
2026-03-10 19:25 - BrightChat (customer): Confirmed they shipped mobile SDK v2.4.1 at 18:22 UTC that changed keepalive behavior. They're pausing rollout and standing by for mitigation.

2026-03-10 19:40 - Diego (SRE): We see accept_queue backlog and many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT/HALF-CLOSED. Spinning up mitigations: throttling short sessions for this tenant and bumping ephemeral-proxy fd soft limit.
2026-03-11 02:15 - BrightChat: After mitigation we see client experience improved; error rate reduced drastically. Thank you. They're still on pause for the SDK rollout.
2026-03-11 03:20 - Lena Chen (Runtime): Merged runtime defensive checks to staging; asking infra to schedule hotfix to the dedicated pool control plane for us-east-1.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Diego (SRE): Hotfix rolled to affected Dedicated pool in us-east-1 at 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC. Monitoring shows stable 5xx baseline. Preparing postmortem.
2026-03-12 10:15 - Aisha (Support): Notifying BrightChat of permanent mitigations and recommended SDK rollback. Closing loop with customer for confirmation before final resolution.
2026-03-12 11:00 - BrightChat: Confirmed they rolled back SDK to v2.4.0 and error rates remain normal. Requesting timeline for permanent fixes and a runbook for future outbreaks.
resolution: Mitigation applied: ingress short-lived-session throttling for BrightChat tenant and soft limit increase on ephemeral proxies. Hotfix deployed to runtime to detect and close half-closed sockets and to short-circuit excessive short-lived sessions per tenant. Customer rolled back problematic SDK. Long-term: add tenant-level short-session throttling default, expand tests for keepalive regressions, and add runbook.
